title: Redwood x CloudMart Marketplace Integration - Technical Sync
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Start: 10:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood Product), Aisha Khan (CloudMart Partnerships), Lucas Reed (CloudMart Marketplace PM), Hiro Tanaka (Cloud Architect)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, well kick off in a minute. I think we have enough folks. Quick agenda: marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for private listings, joint solutions and co-marketing assets, and then next steps and a pilot checklist.

[00:25] Aisha: Sounds good. Appreciate you all making time, we are on a tight partner launch calendar for Q3 so trying to lock down the technical bits.

[00:35] Priya: Ill do a quick run through of integration touchpoints from our side and call out known constraints with VPC/private deployments and listing metadata. Note w. the product names sometimes get swapped in our notes - I may say Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private interchangeably, sorry for that.

[00:55] Lucas: No worries. Our integration owner is Hiro, hell speak to the infra patterns. We also have marketplace onboarding checklists which require: logo and partner description, a technical integration doc, reference architecture diagram, and verified billing/usage telemetry.

[01:20] Hiro: Quick context: CloudMart supports private listings in our marketplace (customers can spin up private SaaS connectors tied to their account) and we need to know what network topology Redwood expects, certs, and whether Redwood offers a connector or we need to build a managed integration.

[01:40] Priya: From Redwoods side there are two common models: hosted API listing (standard marketplace listing, we route through Redwood hosted) and private deployment listing (we provide a VPC connector or on-prem package that sits in the customer's VPC). For the private path we have a reference architecture that uses a private control plane and a customer-managed data plane.

[02:10] Jordan: For the marketplace listing we also need to agree on the pricing presentation — CloudMart shows per-hour or per-seat pricing, while Redwood historically bills per token and has committed capacity options. We'll need to translate/represent our Dedicated/reserved capacity options in marketplace terms.

[02:35] Lucas: Right, we can surface "monthly reserved capacity" as a billing SKU. Well need an example SOW or pricing table to put in the listing.

[02:50] [03:00] Priya: Technical bits: for private listings the main requirements weve seen are: SSO (SAML/OIDC), audit logging, KMS integration for key management, and support for region restrictions (data residency). Are those aligned with CloudMart needs?

[03:20] Aisha: Yes, all of those. Also we'd need to see SOC2 type statements and a short security checklist to attach to the listing.

[03:35] Samir: We have a Redwood security one-pager and SOC2 attestation we can attach, and our KMS/HSM integrations are documented. Well share the security pack after the call.

[03:50] [04:00] Hiro: On networking: does Redwood require inbound connections to customer infra or does the customer reach out to Redwood endpoints? For a marketplace-managed private listing we prefer the "pull" model where the customer agents initiate egress to Redwood so no inbound firewall openings.

[04:20] Priya: We support both but recommend egress-initiated for security. For on-prem deployments there's an installable package that talks outbound to Redwood control plane. For fully air-gapped customers, we can offer an on-prem bundle but that triggers additional validation and longer timelines.

[04:45] Lucas: Good, egress model is ideal. Can you confirm ports, certs, and whether we need to exchange client certs?

[04:55] Priya: Standard TLS 443, mTLS optional. We support token-based auth for control plane registration and optional client certs for extra security. We'll add specifics in the integration doc.

[05:20] [05:30] Jordan: Another thing: telemetry and usage reporting. CloudMart wants to show per-tenant usage in the marketplace UI and enable Marketplace billing. We need to ensure we can emit per-tenant usage hooks or a daily usage report.

[05:45] Hiro: Can we do webhook based usage? We need near-daily reporting to reconcile billing.

[05:55] Samir: We provide usage webhooks and also an S3 export option. Webhooks are better for near real-time marketplace billing. There might be edge cases with batching/kv-cache (I sometimes see us write "KV cash") where token attribution is tricky for prefix-cached sessions; we'll flag that in the doc.

[06:20] [06:30] Lucas: Understood. Also marketplace requires a reference architecture diagram. Do you have a template we can use?

[06:40] Priya: Yes, we'll share a CloudMart-specific reference architecture: three variants — Hosted API listing, Dedicated (reserved capacity) listing, and Private (VPC/on-prem) listing. Each diagram includes network flows, auth pattern (SAML/OIDC, mTLS), and integration points for billing/telemetry.

[07:00] Aisha: Can you annotate the private variant with expected latency and recommended instance sizes? Some of our customers are latency sensitive and ask for notes on GPU families.

[07:15] Samir: We can include guidance: typical latency ranges per model family on our hosted service, and a mapping of our Dedicated instance types to GPU families. Well avoid naming every GPU SKU in the listing to keep it simple but include a link to detailed perf profiles.

[07:35] [07:45] Hiro: Integration pattern question: will CloudMart customers authenticate directly with Redwood or via CloudMart as a broker? For private listings we prefer using CloudMart as broker so the marketplace can manage provisioning.

[07:55] Priya: We support brokered provisioning via a Marketplace API. The flow is: customer buys listing -> CloudMart calls Redwood Marketplace provisioning API -> Redwood provisions Dedicated or issues a private deployment registration token -> installation completes. Well provide an onboarding API spec.

[08:20] Jordan: On the UI side - to certify the listing CloudMart asks for sample demo data and a short walkthrough. We can provide a sandbox tenant access and a test API key for their QA team.

[08:40] Lucas: Great. Regarding joint solutions: we'd like to co-author a reference architecture blog and a joint solution brief highlighting "Redwood Private on CloudMart" for regulated customers. Any constraints on co-branding or logos?

[08:55] Aisha: We'll share CloudMart branding guidelines. Redwood, do you have approved partner logo variants?

[09:05] Samir: Yes, we have a partner logo kit. We'll share that and any co-marketing approvals needed.

[09:20] [09:30] Priya: A few technical caveats to call out that sometimes get missed in marketplace integration: 1) token attribution for multi-tenant prefix caching, 2) model variant fallback behavior when Dedicated capacity is exhausted, 3) latency SLOs for small vs large seq lengths. We'll document these clearly.

[09:55] Hiro: For model fallback, it's important we surface in the marketplace UI whether the listing supports automatic fallback to hosted models (and any associated pricing). Some enterprise customers require data never leave their VPC, that rules out fallback.

[10:15] Jordan: We'll add a property to the listing metadata to indicate "fallback allowed: true/false" and provide copy for the listing to explain behavior.

[10:35] [10:45] Lucas: Security review: we need your pen test window and a contact for security questionnaires.

[10:55] Samir: Send vendor security questionnaire to security@redwood.com and ccing our security lead. Pen test windows are quarterly; we can coordinate a mutually available slot.

[11:10] Aisha: Timeline question: Given Q3 launch target, what are realistic deadlines for docs, integration test, and a pilot?

[11:25] Priya: If we get the marketplace onboarding form this week, we can deliver the integration spec and reference diagrams in 5 business days, a sandbox tenant within 7, and a pilot checklist in 10. Onboarding agents and private deployables may add 3-6 weeks depending on air-gap requirements.

[11:50] [12:00] Hiro: Sounds good. For pilot wed run a small set of customers against the private listing to validate provisioning and usage reporting. Can Redwood provide a short smoke-test plan?

[12:10] Samir: Yes, we have a pilot smoke-test template (will share). It includes provisioning, auth flows (SAML/OIDC), usage webhook validation, and load test at small QPS to confirm billing attribution.

[12:30] Lucas: About legal/billing: CloudMart needs a sample contract language for reserved capacity commitments.

[12:40] Jordan: We'll share a sample SOW and a billing appendix that maps Redwood pricing to a marketplace SKU. Legal review may take a week.

[12:55] [13:00] Priya: Quick note on docs: well put a single URL repo with: README, network diagram, API spec, security pack, and a small runbook for provisioning. We'll push that to a shared CloudMart partner folder.

[13:20] Aisha: Perfect. Anything else?

[13:30] Jordan: Ill recap next steps and owners. Thanks all.

End transcript.
summary: Partner technical sync covering marketplace listing requirements, private listing reference architectures (hosted vs dedicated vs private), networking/auth patterns (egress preferred, TLS/mTLS, SSO), telemetry and billing hooks (webhooks, S3 export), security artifacts (SOC2, pen test, KMS), co-marketing assets, and a pilot timeline to target Q3 launch.
topics: networking and auth (egress, TLS, mTLS, SAML/OIDC)
action_items: Jordan Ellis - Share sample SOW and billing appendix by 2026-07-19
Priya Nair - Deliver integration spec and reference diagrams by 2026-07-22
Samir Gupta - Send security pack and SOC2 attestation to CloudMart security contact by 2026-07-16
Redwood - Provide sandbox tenant credentials and pilot smoke-test plan by 2026-07-23
next_steps: CloudMart to submit marketplace onboarding form by 2026-07-17
Redwood to supply integration artifacts and logo kit
Schedule a follow-up integration review (30-45 min) week of 2026-07-27
